entries.content: The Great City of Demacia, Demacia City, or Great City is located in the western part of the kingdom of Demacia. It is the capital and the home of most noble houses of Demacia. Galio is stationed just outside of the capital. The capital, located in the western part of Demacia, is the main political, cultural, religious, military, economic and educational center of the country. Towering spires punctuate its skyline; Petricite (a pale, magic-resistant stone) and marble are the materials of choice. The noble houses that reside within the city include Buvelle, Crownguard and Laurent. The Royal Palace of House Lightshield is from which the king of Demacia reigns. The city also has a barracks and a penitentiary, like most cities throughout the kingdom. The Capital itself sits next to a natural port overlooking the Conqueror's Sea, with the majority of the surrounding towns resting on a plateau. The Last Gate and Noble Family Residences are located in the Northen part of the city. East Demacia City: Geographical southern part of the city, The Silverwing Aviaries and the religious part of the city are located in the Easten part. The City Harbor is located in the Southern part of the city, situated on its own rocky island and connected via constructed bridge. The Military District and Magessekers Complex are located in western part of the city. The heart of the city has the Kingdoms royal palace known as Citadel of Dawn, Grand Plaza of open courtyard and gardens and the Alabaster Library.

entries.name: Petricite
entries.content: Petricite is a magical material produced in Demacia from petrified trees that can dispel magic, and mixed its wood with ash and lime into a resistant material. It is used everywhere in the nation, from architecture to weapons, and even in the construction of golems. Durand was a great petricite inventor and architect who designed and built Galio, as well as many other petricite structures and objects during the kingdom's foundation. Durand's descendants continue his work in modern times.

entries.name: Petricite Grove
entries.content: Petricite Grove is forest area located on the footholds of the Rocky Highlands of northern Demacia. One of many similar forests in Demacia, it is the location of the rare petrified flora with magical absorbing properties. Deep beneath the ancient petricite groves, Ryze has found a forgotten vault where the volatile energies of the World Rune shards can be safely contained.

entries.name: Petricite Tree
entries.content: Petricite Trees are fossilized-like trees that were magically altered by World Runes. They have magic-dampening abilities as well as the ability to absorb magic. Several stories high, these white trees and their yellow leaves are as hard as stone. However, they are a limited resources as the trees have stopped growing at the moment. Petricite can be ground up and mixed with liquid to make Petricite Elixir.

entries.name: Mageseekers
entries.content: The Mageseeker are a Demacian order tasked with containing magic within the country, hunting down mages, securing magical artifacts and accompanying any magical envoys during their stay in Demacia. If "magical affliction" is noticed in children, they were registered under the Laws of Stone and required to follow its tenets or were given the opportunity to work as Mageseekers themselves.

entries.name: Noxus
entries.content: Noxus is a powerful and expansionist empire that thrives on strength and ambition, where anyone can rise through the ranks based on their abilities. It located on east of Valoran and Demacia, it's capital being Noxus Prime. To those beyond its borders, Noxus is brutal, expansionist, and threatening, yet those who look beyond its warlike exterior see an unusually inclusive society, where the strengths and talents of its, where the strengths and talents of its people are respected and cultivated, even accepting magic. Noxians are deeply proud people who value strength above all, though that strength can manifest by many different means. Anyone can rise to a position of power and respect within Noxus if they display the necessary aptitude, regardless of social standing, background, homeland, or wealth. Their form of government is called Trifarix, ruled by three people of importance, including the Grand General, Jericho Swain. Noxus will do anything to win wars, including heinous crimes, using forbidden magic, reviving the dead and commissioning chemical weapons from Zaun. Despite this meritocratic ideal, the old noble families still wield considerable power in the empire. As Noxus expands and defeats neighboring cultures and cities, it offers the conquered people a choice; swear loyalty to Noxus and be judged solely on your worth, or be destroyed. Noxus meritocracy is exemplified by the Trifarix doctrine. This is made up of three core aspects. Might, Vision, and Guile. Stewards are the provincial rulers of Noxus, tasked to enforce Noxian rule in occupied territories as well as cities.

entries.name: Noxus Prime
entries.content: Noxus Prime is the sprawling capital city of the Empire of Noxus. Located on the river delta in eastern Noxus, the city was built on top of an old fortification known as The Immortal Bastion. The Immortal Bastion was built by a dreaded sorcerer sorcerer in a far distant age. Within the stronghold's walls, the streets and alleyways are narrow and twisting. The rooftops are flat and crenelated, like the battlements of a castle. Many noble houses are located in the capital. The city is also the headquarters of the enigmatic Black Rose cabal. Mortoraa is a small district within the Immortal Bastion, known for being one of the wealthiest neighborhoods. The streets in Mortoraa are luxurious and comfortably spacious. However, at night it has a reputation as the most ominous district for the streets are never illuminated with torch-light or lanterns; Bastion Center Tri-Towers is at the center of the Bastion, it is a place forbidden by the order of the Trifarix due to it not being under their control. It's the headquarter of the Black Rose; Shrine of the Wolf is tall, multi-tiered tower with open sides, butting up against the old southern bulwarks of the Immortal Bastion. In the center of the tower, looming almost fifty feet high, is a massive obsidian statue of a seated wolf; Stairs of Triumph are long unbroken flight of stairs leading to the Audience Chamber. Going to the Audience Chamber, a pair of liveried Legionnaires clad in dark steel stand sentinel every twelve steps.

entries.name: Noble Houses of Noxus
entries.content: Noble Houses of Noxus are the following: House Cortain, house whose known member is part of the Crimson Circle; House Darkwill, a family that was the ruling house of Noxus before the Trifarix; House Du Couteau, a house that rules one of the largest assassin guilds in Noxus, with historic ties to the Black Rose. Matron Soreana is secretly part of the cabal; House Granth; House  Kythera-Zaavan, a house unionized by two noble houses, Kythera and Zaavan, orchestrated with meticulous care by Elise, the former matron of House Kythera, through a strategically arranged marriage; House Mallat, a house with ties to the Black Rose and Mordekaiser; House Noradi, a house whose known members are part of the Crimson Circle; House Sassen; House Swain, one of the first noble houses in Noxus, with historic ties to Black Rose. Most if not all other members were executed after Jericho exposed them for plotting against the empire; House Tewain, noble house responsible for gaining favor of numerous Minotaur clans before claiming Basilich.

entries.name: Trifarix
entries.content: The Trifarix, also known as the "Council of Three", is the current governing body of Noxus. Noxus is governed by a triad of equal leaders known as the Council of Three, each representing one of the core Principles of Strength. Members are: Darius, the Hand of Noxus and Commander of the elite Trifarian Legion. Jericho Swain, the Noxian Grand General and face of government for the Empire. And The Faceless, the indenity is officially a mystery. But the puppeteer of the dark underbelly and politics of Noxus is LeBlanc.

entries.name: Black Rose
entries.content: Black Rose is a secret organization in primarily stationed Noxus. The Leader of Black Rose Cabal is LeBlanc. Black Rose Cabal's purpose is guiding Noxus from the shadows and Preventing/Defeating Mordekaiser. The Black Rose is a secretive cabal led by the Noxian aristocracy with it's influence reaching all of Noxus and beyond it's borders. Many of their opulent designs feature masks so that they can partially conceal their identities, even from each other. Remnants of an order that has existed far longer than Noxus itself, initiates of the Black Rose have schemed from the shadows for centuries, guiding the throne of Noxus for more than a thousand years, orchestrating many of the empire's most ambitious campaigns. The Black Rose exists now to further the clandestine interests of those who can wield the magic hidden within the Immortal Bastion, with its rank-and-file composed of mundane nobles. Even the most powerful military commander could only ever serve the cult's true masters. Champions of The Black Rose are it's leader LeBlanc along with Lord Vladimir, Elise and Cassiopeia.

entries.name: Crimson Circle
entries.content: The Crimson Circle is an exclusive secret order of Noxus. All of its members are hemomancy users devoted to their patron, Lord Vladimir. Under Vladimir's tutelage, the art of hemomancy has found a place in the military of Noxus, and among scions of the old aristocracy. Among these diverse practitioners is the Crimson Circle, a youthful cult dedicated as much to Vladimir's personality as to blood magic itself. The purpose of the cult is Furthering dedication to the practition of Blood Magic and Revering Lord Vladimir. Crimson Circle has connections to the Black Rose Cabal, as Lord Vladimir is Patron of the Black Rose.

entries.name: Trifarian Legion
entries.content: The Trifarian Legion is the most elite military order of Noxus. The most elite and loyal legion in modern Noxus. Lead by Darius, it takes a ruthlessly discerning eye to select those worthy enough to become part of the Trifarian Legion, but they can sort the sheep from the wolves a mile away. The Legion spread the empire's reach with every beat of their drums. Not exclusively made from Noxian born citizens, everyone can join the Trifarian Legion if they prove themselves.

entries.name: Mount Targon
entries.content: Mount Targon is a mountainous region to the west of Shurima, Targon boasts the tallest peak in Runeterra.Targon is where people worship celestial entities. It is home to powerful beings called the Aspects, and many seek to ascend Mount Targon to gain immense power. If anyone manages to climb to the top, they'll be blessed with divine powers and become an Aspect. There's two main religious groups opposing each other: the Solari who worship the sun, and the Lunaria, who worship the moon and are persecuted by the former. Located far from civilization, Mount Targon is all but impossible to reach, save by the most determined pilgrims. Those hardy few who survive the arduous journey to the foot of the titanic mountain find a sky shimmering with celestial bodies, constellations, planets, fiery comets that streak the darkness, and auspicious arrangements of stars. Mount Targon is simply a way into the celestial realm. Mount Targon can be broken into distinct regions, as delineated by patterns in the rock and a marked increase in hazardous weather conditions, difficulty of the climb, and increased death rate. The upper levels of the mountain expand and contract as if the land itself were alive, making it impossible to map a reliable pathway to the top.

entries.name: Astral Grove
entries.content: Astral Grove is located in the upper slopes south of Mount Targon. It is where Soraka resides, it has a campfire and a little yurt with few items and souvenirs from all across Runeterra.

entries.name: Marus Omegnum
entries.content: Marus Omegnum, also known as LoR Non-Champion Non-Spell Indicator The Veiled Temple, is a full Lunari temple fortress located for the majority of the time inside the Spirit Realm. During special lunar events, the temple phases into the physical realm and shows up on Mount Targon.

entries.name: Targon Prime
entries.content: Described as a brilliant city of gold and silver, Targon Prime is a realm beyond Runeterra where celestial beings known as Aspects and mythical creatures of the stars reside. Every generation or so, an Aspect will descend from Targon Prime to imbue mortals, whom they deem worthy, to become their vessel. It is a vast realm bathed in golden light at day and sparkling stars at night. Currently Kayle has set out for this realm, to learn what has really happened to her mother Mihira. Sometimes the reason for these Targonian Ascended's disappearances can be linked to Targon Prime on which deceased aspect vessels are now a part of the great council planning to build an army of powerful human-celestial mieldings against the unknowable nothingness. In the rare event that a mortal reaches Targon’s peak, the heavens open before them in a dazzling display of cosmic aurorae. Few ever bear witness to that radiant sight, far above the cloudline and beneath the glittering stars, where it is said that timeless, godlike beings dwell in a wondrous city of gold and silver. The Aspects live in Targon Prime. Some of the inhabitants are Diana, the Ascended host to the Aspect of the Moon; Ezreal, influenced by the Aspect of the Wanderer; Leona, the Ascended host to the Aspect of the Sun; Morgana, the offspring of the current host of the Aspect of Justice and is also Kayle's sister; Atreus the reborn Aspect of War; Soraka, a wandering fallen celestial caretaker; Taric, the Ascended host to the Aspect of the Protector.

entries.name: Aspects
entries.content: The Aspects are stellar beings that live beyond the physical and spiritual realms of Runeterra in the cosmic realm of Targon Prime. These beings embody concepts and celestial magics. They are able to meld with mortals, ascend them, making them their hosts with which they are able to traverse and / or interact with the mortal plane with relative efficiency. However, with the exception of the Aspect of Twilight Aspect of Twilight and its hosts they rarely interfere with the mortal realm outside of time with great needs. Aspect remain among the most powerful beings in the Universe.

entries.name: Aspect Host
entries.content: The term Aspect Host refers to humans magically altered and usually made hosts to the Aspects of Targon Prime. Blessed with incredible strength, speed and a strong affinity for mastering forms of magic. The Aspect hosts are also virtually immune to pain and sickness. Some have their lifespan dramatically increased. But they can still bleed, be crippled, or even killed with the right weapon, magic, or overwhelming force. After each host dies and during times of great needs, the Aspect finds a new host to replace their place.

entries.name: God-Warrior
entries.content: The God-Warriors are the ascended of Shurima. The God-warriors, also known as the Sunborn, were once Shuriman ascended who underwent a transformative ritual to give them extraordinary power and long life so they could safeguard their nation and its interests.

entries.name: Ascended
entries.content: The umbrella term Ascended refers to all humans who were magically altered by a variety of magic, chiefly celestial magic. After their ascension, the Ascended can channel celestial magic through their connection to celestial entities, but do not "gain" celestial magic themselves.

entries.name: Piltover
entries.content: Piltover is one of the two interconnected cities. Piltover, known as the City of Progress, is a thriving, progressive and advanced city. A city of inventors and scientists, with a steampunk level of technology, resembling victorian england. It's Valoran's cultural center, where art, craftsmanship, trade and innovation walk hand in hand. Its power comes not through military might, but the engines of commerce and forward thinking. It's situated on the cliffs above the district of Zaun and overlooking the ocean. The wealth this generates has given rise to an unprecedented boom in the city's growth. Burgeoning merchant clans fund development in the most incredible endeavors: grand artistic follies, esoteric hextech research, and architectural monuments to their power. With ever more inventors delving into the emergent lore of hextech, Piltover has become a lodestone for the most skilled craftsmen the world over. They harness magic to power machines, known as Hextech. The most influential individuals of Piltover live and rule in the Bluewind Court, located in northern Piltover. Mainspring Crescent is fashionable promenade of cafes, bistros, and supper clubs. Trade is the lifeblood of Piltover, and its command of the main sea-route between east and west has seen its coffers swell with gold. The climate around Piltover is generally balmy, but when the temperature changes rapidly, sea fogs often envelop the docks and warehouses. The citizen of Piltover are typically self-reliant, does not expect handouts, uptight, and always aspires to do better.

entries.name: Zaun
entries.content: Zun is one of the two interconnected cities. Zaun is a large undercity district to Piltover, separated by a river and a canyon that goes deep into the ground. Zaun is industrial, chaotic, and home to dangerous experiments with chemtech and chem-barons. What light reaches below is filtered through fumes and reflected from green stained glass. Zaun thrives and its people vibrant and its culture rich. Deeply polluted and impoverished, most of it's people are blue collar workers. Drugs, crime and misery runs rampant. Immoral mad scientists come here to experiment. The people of Zaun resent Piltover deeply. They have developed their own form of technology called chemtech, which uses dangerous chemicals. It's way more unstable and risky than Hextech, but potentially more powerful. Promenade Level is where entertainment and commercial zone. This is where the wealthy of Zaun gather to shop, dine, and trade goods and supplies from below and where Pilties go for good, cheap times. Entresol Level of Zaun situated just below the Promenade. Deep in Zaun, brokers, dealers, traffickers and entertainers mingle in cliff-dug trading posts and workshops. A flourishing hub of cosmopolitan commercial arcades, supper-clubs, recital halls, joy houses. Sump Level is Zaun's deepest levels, past the reaches of the Gray-filtered light, the environment turns grim, increasingly disorderly, and poorly lit. Most of the working class live here or just above it. While known to be notoriously self-centered people, the denizens of Zaun collectively take great pride in themselves.

entries.name: Stillwater Hold
entries.content: Stillwater Hold is a prison complex on an island off the southern coast of Piltover and Zaun. Stillwater holds several criminals captured in Piltover and Zaun. The fort goes up to at least 40 floors, and has cells for solitary confinement. The prisoners are also given tasks, such as cleaning the roof, around the prison and have time allotted for mandatory exercise.

entries.name: Shimmer
entries.content: Shimmer is a potent and corrosive techmaturgical, serum-like substance with a wide range of uses. It is popular amongst Zaun's rebellious youth and was distributed as a street drug during Silco's reign over the undercity. Much like the flowers it was created from, shimmer is a bright purple liquid that radiates a soft, purple glow. It is addictive and flammable, producing bright pink flames as it burns. Although most users tend to either drink the drug directly or inject it into the bodies using syringes, it can also be inhaled in gas form. In small quantities, shimmer can accelerate the healing process and enhance the user's physical constitution. In larger amounts, it can grant superhuman levels of strength, speed, and durability. A full dose can cause the user to temporarily grow dramatically in size; but it's extremely painful. Those who use shimmer in this manner seem to display a sharp loss in cognitive abilities and increased aggression. Frequent use of Shimmer can cause progressive degeneration of the skin and muscle tissue. Overuse can lead to permanent physical deformities.

entries.name: Hextech
entries.content: Hextech is a magical technology that fuses elemental and spirit magic to create exquisite artifacts that can be wielded by anyone. It harnesses the magical power contained within rare hex crystals to function properly. Hextech's power is limited only by the imagination of their users and is capable of amazing feats. Hextech devices have runes inscribed on them; when the runes are coupled with the power of the hextech gemstones, it gives the device its magical properties. The process of crafting hextech is a closely guarded secret, and no two artificers work to the same methodology.

entries.name: Wardens
entries.content: The Wardens, or the Enforcers, are the law enforcement organization in Piltover, funded by trade taxes and 'generous' contributions from the mercantile clans. The Department presumably has a number of departments and ranks under it. Their duties range from investigating and arresting criminals, patrolling Zaun and Piltover's streets, as well as the Academy and Council building, watching over events in the city and their high-ranking officials, serving as prisonguards of Stillwater Hold, guarding the ports and inspecting shipments, enforcing orders and laws as imposed by Councilors, among many others. Enforcers have blue armor with golden trims, helmets that can full-face gasmask attached and are usually armed with batons and rifles.

entries.name: Bilgewater
entries.content: Bilgewater is chaotic port city east of Piltover and Zaun, across the sea. Bilgewater is filled with pirates, sea monsters, traders, dock-gangs, indigenous peoples, and traders from across the known world. It’s a haven for those who seek freedom and fortune on the high seas. Almost anything can be purchased here, from outlawed hextech to the favor of local crime lords. It's a melting pot of cultures, races, and creeds, alive with activity at all hours. There is no better place to seek fame and fortune, though death lurks in every alleyway, and the law is almost non-existent. The surrounding ocean is populated by terrifying sea monsters that are hunted for a living. It's ruled by Pirate Captains and the strongest of them all is Miss Fortune, the Queen of Bilgewater. Cutpurse Square is a thriving marketplace surrounded by swaying dwellings built in a wide square on one of the floating wharf-shanties. Bilgewater Bay is the main entrance to the largest settlement of Bilgewater, Rat Town. Butcher's Bridge, which is located upstream and above the Slaughter Docks. Fleet Street has various pubs and taverns and boasts the island's finest rum. In Bilgewater one can come across many astounding creatures brought from the dark and mysterious Guardian's Sea, such as dragon-sharks, sea serpents, giant squid, four-eyed hammerhead sharks, and kraken. There are also more mundane creatures such as octopi, hammerhead sharks, devilfish, clams, and ordinary fish.

entries.name: Bilgewater Bay
entries.content: Bilgewater Bay is an island location, the main coastal settlement of Bilgewater and the largest settlement on the Serpent Isles. A natural harbor in the Blue Flame Isles. Its many haphazard settlements make up the greater city of Bilgewater, a renowned haven for criminal activity in the region. Surrounded by treacherous straits and towering cliffs, Bilgewater Bay is as dangerous as those who call it home. Situated in the lowest parts of Bilgewater Bay, these locations are the primary location of Bilgewater's black market. Bilgewater's lowliest inhavitants dwell in a labyrinth of meandering canals and hidden inlets. Bilgewater Bay is the main entrance to the largest settlement of Bilgewater, Rat Town. Butcher's Bridge, which is located upstream and above the Slaughter Docks, acts as a gate to the inner parts of the city as well as the bridge to the Temple of the Mother Serpent. Because of the cities' mixed cultural heritage, the area boasts a wide variety of architectural designs, from inverted Freljordian logships against the carved cliff-faces to the structures and carvings of the indigenous population. Fleet Street has various pubs and taverns and boasts the island's finest rum.

entries.name: Serpent Isles
entries.content: Serpent Isles, or Blue Flame Isles, is an island archipelago off the southeastern coast of the Valoran mainland. Notably, it contains Bilgewater. The culture of Serpent Isles is deeply tied to Bilgewater. Bilgewater, over the years, has become an important stop for trade ships traveling near the Serpent Isles. While much of Valoran knows the archipelago as the Blue Flame Isles, to the indigenous people of Buhru they have only ever been the Serpent Isles. Buhru's ancient culture is highly respected, reflected, and sometimes imitated in the daily life of Bilgewater, including traditional medicine, and monster hunting techniques. Buhru is part of the larger Serpent Isles.

entries.name: Buhru
entries.content: Buhru is an island and coastal settlement which is part of the larger Serpent Isles. Here battle isn't considered a test of strength, but of will. These Isles are the location from which the religion of Nagakabouros and its priestess, Illaoi, originate from.

entries.name: Shuriman Continent
entries.content: Shuriman Continent is the southern continent of Runeterra. Desertic land east of Mount Targon, similar to the Egyptian empire in aesthetics and themes. Deeply magical, with their own demigods called the Ascended. The most predominant nation on this continent is Shurima from which it gained its name. This continent is now connected to Valoran through a small artificial land bridge where modern day Piltover and Zaun are located. Some of the nations and city-states here are the Hidden city of the Ixtali, the Fallen desert empire Shurima  and Sprawling western mountains of Targon.

entries.name: Shurima
entries.content: The empire of Shurima is a vast desert empire with a rich history of ancient gods and Ascended warriors. Recently reborn, it seeks to reclaim its former glory with the rise of Azir. Over millennia, tales of Shurima's glorious city became myth and religion among the descendants of the scattered survivors. Most of the nomadic nomadic inhabitants of Shurima search for basic sustenance in an unforgiving land. Some defend small outposts built around a few oases. Others hunt buried riches among the ruins of the fallen empire, or obtain mercenary mercenary work, taking coin for their deeds before disappearing back into the sands. Now, the tribes are stirred by whispers from the heart of the desert: the city of Shurima has risen risen again. Shurima is described as a place that had a thriving culture, not only a strong military and a powerful emperor. It had a sense of personal identity with art, music, literature, trade, magical technology and more. The people of Shurima have been emperors and warriors, slaves and scholars, enduring beneath the glare of the deser sun. Through their knowledge of the sands, their strong family bonds, and sheer determination that history will not forget them, they have survived wars that spanned many centuries.

entries.name: Sun Disc
entries.content: The Sun Disc is a megastructure built in the center of the Shuriman Continent and functions as the ancient and modern capital of Shurima. Built with the aid of Mount Targon and Ixtal, the Sun Disc is the primary mechanism for the creation of the God-Warriors. Damaged during Xerath's ascension, it has recently been repaired with the resurrection and ascension of Azir. For eons, the sun worshippers of Shurima owed their society's prosperity to the incredible power of the sun. Thanks to the prodigious disk that hovered above the capital city, ancient Shurimans could wield raw celestial magic to make their land more bountiful. The Sun Disc was the center of all Shuriman culture; it permeated every aspect, from religion to icons to dress and so on. Because of its immense importance as the center of trade and culture of the empire, many cultural, educational centers and markets bringing goods from all over the Empire sprung up. It also housed special burial grounds for the most influential of its citizens, such as The Tomb of the Emperors. The city is divided by ringed districts and city levels. The city's wealthiest citizens lived in the top rings of the city, while middle and lower classes (with slaves) lived mostly in settlements built on the rocky cliff sides of the outer and lower rings. The Palace of Ten Thousand Pillars, Scholar's Palace, Temple of the Sun and Oasis of the Dawn are located at the center of the city. The most important road in the city was the Emperor's Way. The city was built around the ancient Sun Disc that floats above The Circle of Ascension and the city itself. The city also had the most advanced irrigation system of its time, seemingly unsurpassed until recently. Floating gardens decorated with palms and other flora protected its many terraces from the burning sun.

entries.name: Ixtal
entries.content: Ixtal is renowned for its mastery of elemental magic, located in the Tropical jungles south of Zaun and in the east parts of Shurima. Ixtal's capital is Ixaocan and their religion is Axiomata. It's government is Magical Autocracy, with ruled by Yun Tal Caste System and Vastayan Councils. The Mage Autocracy functions on a caste system where every person has a set role in society. An individual can rarely change their caste and are often within a caste for their entire life. The mages of Ixtal distanced themselves from their neighbors. Secluded deep in the jungle for thousands of years, the sophisticated arcology-city of Ixaocan remains mostly free of outside influence. Having witnessed from afar the ruination of the Blessed Isles and the Rune Wars that followed, the Ixtali view all the other factions of Runeterra as upstarts and pretenders, and use their powerful magic to keep any intruders at bay. Many Vastaya live here, and powerful elemental mages. The jungles of Ixtal are dotted with multiple outlying villages and settlements, separate from the arcologies of Ixaocan. The most trusted Yun Tal may be designated as the prefects of these villages. They would resolve local disputes, test potential aspirants, and generally ensure that the Ixtali people have as little interaction with outsiders as possible. The Yun Tal closed the Ixtali border by drawing the wilderness around them to act as a barrier, isolating Ixaocan and its surrounding jungles from the rest of Runeterra. The barrier erected by the Yun Tal, manifests several potent effects like Elemental magic manipulates the weather, conjuring sudden storms that persist for days, drenching intruders and making navigation treacherous. The dense mist obscures visibility, leading travelers astray, while the landscape itself shifts and rearranges, impeding progress and trapping those who venture within.

entries.name: Ixaocan
entries.content: Ixaocan is a system of arcologies that stretches across the jungles of Ixtal. The Cardinal Arcology, sometimes also named after the system it anchors, stands as its heart. The arcologies are connected by intersecting lines of power, and each represents a specific form or discipline of elemental magic. The largest are home to tens of thousands of Ixtali practitioners. However, they are neither wholly habitats nor colleges of magic, but something in between. The Cardinal Arcology is the center piece of the system and houses the seat of the Yun Tal. The gargantuan structure was sculpted by Skarner as a gift to the Ixtali people for their devotion. It has stood since before the ancient Shurimans raised their first Sun Disc in Nerimazeth. Within the cardinal arcology of Ixaocan is a grand chamber, deliberately positioned at the very center of Ixtal. Above this chamber hangs the Vidalion, an ancient artifact that can weave magic into material form. Beneath Ixaocan lies a secret chamber home to Skarner, a founding member of the Yun Tal, and protector of Ixtal. Here he lies, attuned to the earth's vibrations, vigilant for any threats to Ixtal. Only the Yun Tal are aware of Skarner's presence beneath the city.

entries.name: Magma Arcology
entries.content: High in the mountains of Ixtal, the mages of this relatively small arcology combine their understandings of fire, rock, and magnetism to draw precious metals from the earth, crafting them into exquisite shapes with the merest gesture.

entries.name: Water Arcology
entries.content: Located next to one of the many river confluences of the Serpentine River of Ixtal, the mages of this arcology combine their understandings of water, ice, and steam to reshape the land around them.

entries.name: Yun Tal
entries.content: The Yun Tal are the self-ruling Ixaocan caste of Ixtal, and sort of the Nobility. For countless generations, Ixtal's secrets have been preserved by their most gifted and wise elementalists. There are no formal criteria for admission to the Yun Tal, though aspirants can expect to be tested to the very limit of their abilities, and any approval must be unanimous among those present. Each Yun Tal caste member wears special elemental clothing woven from the Vidalion to enhance and showcase their elemental prowess. The current occupants of the high seat of the Yun Tal were blessed with ten daughters, respectfully referred to by many as “the Yunalai”. Having the benefit of generations of inherited mastery, all of them were ready to face the Vidalion at prodigiously young ages. One of its members, Qiyana, desires to break her position within the caste hierarchy and one day rule as Empress. Its caste members can also hold the position of a prefect.

entries.name: Shadow Islands
entries.content: The land now known as the Shadow Isles was once a beautiful realm and it's capital was once Helia, but it was shattered by a magical cataclysm called the Ruination. It's populated by ghosts, undead, zombies and monsters. Viego, now called the Ruined King, tried to prevent his wife, Isolde, from dying, using the blessed waters of the land. It caused a magical explosion and creation of the Black Mist, which kills everyone it touches and transforms it into a ghost, ghoul or other type of undead creature. This Black Mist permanently shrouds the isles and the land itself is tainted, corrupted by malevolent sorcery. Living beings that stand upon the Shadow Isles slowly have their life-force leeched from them, which draws the insatiable, predatory spirits of the dead and also Wraiths. Those who die within the Black Mist are condemned to haunt the Shadow Isles for eternity. Souls claimed by the Black Mist are known to some as the Fallen. While usually corporeal, they can be harmed with the right tool, such as magic, silver, or even sunlight. The power of the Shadow Isles is waxing stronger with every passing year, allowing the shades of undeath to extend their range and reap souls all across Runeterra. The Black Mist was once the White Mist, merely a natural magical enchantment protecting the Isles of anyone trying to trespass on them. An area called the Undead Wilds is a forest twisted and rotted into grotesque imitation. The Twisted Treeline is located somewhere in the Shadow Isles. It's a forested area houses Arachnids and spirit altars and lair of the Vilemaw.

entries.name: Arachnids
entries.content: Arachnids known as Spiderlings are the giant children of Elise and Vilemaw and reside in both Noxus and the Shadow Isles. Large dark spiders with red highlights, they feast upon the living flesh of humans and other large prey. Living in groups, they gained a hive mind with each other as well as their Spider Queen Elise.

entries.name: Vilemaw
entries.content: Vilemaw is a giant, magical arachnoid being that resides in the Shadow Isles' Twisted Treeline.  This unearthly horror is a monstrous creature that looms in the darkest pits beneath the Shadow Isles. The true origin of Vilemaw is completely unknown, save for the assumption that the voracious spider god is an otherworldly life-form not originally from the Shadow Isles. Resembling a spider whose grotesque mass is furred and scabbed with wet, mutant growths. Adorned with venomous fangs and colossal legs used to heave its corrupt body. It has Immense Physical and Magical Strength.

entries.name: Twisted Treeline
entries.content: The Twisted Treeline is located in the mysterious Shadow Isles. An eternally thick, unnatural fog blankets the islands from the view of outsiders. It is thought that the islands are home to countless forms of undead.

entries.name: Helia
entries.content: Helia is the former capital of the Blessed Isles, reduced to ruins on the Shadow Isles after the Ruination. Helia was once regarded a center of knowledge and learning, in part due to its large archive of Runeterra's artifacts, both dangerous and benign. The city was located on the coast and encompassed several small islands connected through bridges built over waterways. As a result, many parts of the city were flooded after the Ruination. Champions of Helia are Maokai, Thresh, and Yorick.

entries.name: Ionian Archipelago
entries.content: Ionian Archipelago is an Runeterran island chain east from Valoran, north of Bilgewater and east of Noxus across the sea. Previously only the nation of Ionia settled on the archipelago, but in recent history Noxus was able to secure several islands and territories for expansion. The most magical and mystical land of Runeterra, with a culture akin to a mixture of Japanese, Korean and Chinese traditions. People here are connected to nature, since everything has a spirit here. Here the Vastaya are oppressed by humans. It's people are mystical, spiritual and independent. There's still noxian settlements here, and Noxus is planning a second invasion soon.

entries.name: Ionia
entries.content: Ionia is a land of unspoiled beauty and natural magic, located on the Ionian Archipelago, east from Valoran and north of Bilgewater. Its inhabitants, living in scattered settlements across the massive archipelago, are a spiritual people who seek to live in harmony and balance with the world. However, it has endured conflict due to Noxian invasions, leading to a mix of peace-loving monks and war-trained soldiers. There are many orders and sects across Ionia, each following their own often conflicting paths and ideals. Ionia has remained largely neutral, until it was invaded by Noxus. The brutal Noxian conflict and occupation has forced Ionia into militarization and vigilantism. Since Ionian culture has long been shaped by the pursuit of balance in all things, the border between the material and spirit realms tends to be more permeable here, especially in the wild forests and mountains. Now, Ionia exists in an uneasy peace. Some groups, such as the Shojin monks or the Kinkou, seek a return to isolationist pacifism, and pastoral traditions. Other more radical factions, such as the Navori Brotherhood and the Order of Shadow, demand a militarization of the land's magic, to create a single, unified nation that can take vengeance on Noxus. Worshipped religions are Akana Spirits, Kanmei Spirits and Kindred (Lamb & Wolf). Ionia utilize spirit magic regularly. The Spirit Blossom Festival is an ancient and celebrated time in Ionia.

entries.name: Ionia City
entries.content: Ionia City is a large city on which Ionians were gathered and harmonized by the magic that is within the First Lands. Magical Quinlons scatter all across the borders. Like any other nations, the Capital is the seat of power for the Ionian Ruling Council which members include Karma and Irelia.

entries.name: Kinkou Order
entries.content: The Kinkou Order is an ancient organization of Ionia which is dedicated in preserving a balance between the physical world and the spirit realm, without showing a preference to either with it's leader being Shen. The Kinkou Order is an ancient clan originating in the Ionian Isles and are the self-appointed keepers of Ionia's sacred balance. The order's loyal acolytes walk the spirit and material realms, mediating conflicts between them and, when necessary, intervening by force. The Order employs a triumvirate of shadow warriors to uphold its causes in the world. The three warriors are each entrusted with one of three sacred duties: the pure impartiality of Watching the Stars, the passage of judgment in Coursing the Sun, and the elimination of imbalance by Pruning the Tree. The Kinkou Order controls several temples and/or monasteries around Ionia, primarily on the Ionian Mainland of the Navori and Shon-Xan regions.

entries.name: Shadow Order
entries.content: The Yánléi, more widely known as Shadow Order or The Order of Shadows, was founded by Zed and the former disciples of the Kinkou Order. Their task is to protect Ionia and crush any enemy that threatens their rule. Most of the orders members are shadow magic users, sourcing their powers from the Tears of The Shadow artifact from which the order got its name. The Shadow Order controls, several temples and/or monasteries around Ionia, primarily on the Ionian Mainland of the Navori and Shon-Xan regions. Those that master the shadow arts have their bodies physically altered by the use of the magic, some more drastically than others. The Order of Shadows draws their power from shadow tears, a magical ichor which grants them the ability to manipulate shadow magic when tattooed or ingested.

entries.name: Navori Brotherhood
entries.content: The Navori Brotherhood are an ultra-nationalist group established during the Invasion of Noxus. An extremist group looking to militarize Ionia to fight invaders, the Navori Brotherhood is one of many factions with different ideologies springing from the Ionian resistance led by Irelia in the war against Noxus. The Brotherhood in particular became more aggressive when she wasn't the hardcore leader they needed. At some point later, Master Kusho of the Kinkou Order soon became their leader after faking his death with the help of Zed. Although they aim to defend their people from foreign attackers, they also aspire to control the continent under one rule, and are willing to attack and kill fellow Ionians who don't align with their vision for Ionia, including Irelia.

entries.name: Bandle City
entries.content: Bandle is a city out of Runeterra's dimension where the yordles live. In Bandle City, it is said that every sensation is heightened for non-yordles. Colors are brighter. Food and drink intoxicates the senses for years and, once tasted, will never be forgotten. The sunlight is eternally golden, the waters crystal clear, and every harvest brings a fruitful bounty. Deeply magical, chaotic and mysterious in nature. It has portals connecting to all of Runeterra that only the yordles know. While Bandle City has no official form of governance, they do have a mayor. No one recalls Bandle City ever appointing a mayor. He was simply there one day, a plump yordle with a funny hat who decreed this and pontificated that. Any who questioned his legitimacy soon forgot their concerns as he shook hands and twirled his magnificent, stately mustache. The role is simply a self-appointed one with no actual political power or sway towards the yordle inhabitants of the city.

entries.name: The Spirit Blossom Festival
entries.content: The Spirit Blossom Festival is an ancient and celebrated time in Ionia, when the door to the spirit world is opened, the dead return to their loved ones, and spirits of all manner turn their eyes towards the living. From the benevolent Kanmei, to the obsessive Akana. Painters, musicians, calligraphers and other types of artists showcase their artistry to the public, especially children. When nightfall arrives and the Spirit Blossoms are at full bloom, the festival attendees gather at the nearest temple to release lanterns in the air while also giving respect to their fallen and deceased as well as wish for good fortunes. The war and bloodshed of the Noxian Invasion of Ionia had prevented the blossoming of the flowers, but eventually they have returned along with the festival. Some Noxians that live in or near the Noxian occupied areas of Ionia would also join in the festivity, though their presence is still met with some unease.

entries.name: The Void
entries.content: The Void is a purple, nightmarish and infinite dimension that exist outside space and time filled unfettered creation, tortured landscapes of crazed organic machinery, magical weapon-looms and mountainous flesh-forges. It is a force of insatiable hunger, waiting through the eons until its masters, the mysterious Watchers, mark the final time of undoing. Unspeakable abominations, akin to Lovecraftian monsters and gods, inhabit the Void. They have been crossing over to Runeterra, corrupting and mutating everything they touch. Anyone who comes in contact with the Void, it's energy or it's creatures becomes mutated irreversibly, like the darkin. Void Rifts may appear in deep, underground locations that lead into the Void. In places where the Void breaks into Runeterra, it will begin to corrupt or change the landscape.

entries.name: Voidborn
entries.content: Voidborn are beings constructed by the Watchers of The Void. Their reason for existing is to accept, consume, and learn all the information about Runeterra necessary enough to aid for the eventual return of the Watchers. The Voidborn are generally pale, fibrous and flexible. As they age, sections of their form harden into a darker, shell-like chitin, which can become strong enough to turn aside almost any weapon. And no two Voidborn are exactly the same. Voidborn vary greatly in intelligence and development. As such there are also different hierarchies. There are multiple species of voidborn with only two being known: the Xer'Sai and the Zz'Rot. The Xer'Sai run rampant across the Sai Desert, a vast wasteland in southern Shurima, with their queen Rek'Sai being the apex predator of the entire region. The Zz'Rot are diminutive quadrupeds with a volatile biology. The flesh of a voidborn is not edible for humans and decays very fast after their death. One of the few known ways to combat the Void is to starve it. With no organic or magical sustenance nearby, the Void's material growth will slow, until it eventually falls into a dormant state.

entries.name: Xer'Sai
entries.content: Xer'Sai are Voidborn creatures that plague the southern deserts of Shurima. They are the size of big dogs on average, but can be smaller or much bigger. Rek'Sai, as the queen, is by far the largest and most dangerous of her species. The Xer'Sai burst from their small burrows and ravage anything nearby, to the detriment of desert caravans. Once dead, the Xer'Sai decompose at an abnormally rapid rate and become inedible.

entries.name: Lavender Sea
entries.content: The Lavender Sea is an underground realm created by Bel'Veth after consuming and recreating the city of Belveth and its surrounding seas. It has the appearance of a purple sea, hence its name, and has multiple different walls created by material that was consumed by Bel'Veth. It's an Imperial Hivemind led by Bel'Veth.

entries.name: Watcher
entries.content: The Watchers are ancient beings of The Void and the masters above all living Voidborns. While in the Void, the Watchers are formless beings. In the material world, the physical appearance of the Watchers may vary based on their surroundings. In their physical forms, the Watchers are bound by the rules of Runeterra.

entries.name: Darkin
entries.content: Darkin are Shuriman God-Warriors corrupted by the Void, taking the form of demons capable of using blood magic. Extremely dangerous and powerful, capable of killing gods. all known Darkin are confined and trapped inside weapons and various objects, unable to ever regain their original Ascended forms. The Darkin have become imprisoned within their own weapons. The nature of their corruption is after the mental scar left from the horrors of countless wars and those witnessed in the Void War. The death of Azir and the fall of Shurima were the final catalysts that led to them turning their backs to the world they had once swore to protect. Some of the known Darkins are Aatrox, Naafiri, Rhaast and Varus.

entries.name: Yordles
entries.content: The Yordle are a race of spirits who generally take the appearance of mammalian bipeds, akin to gnomes. They mostly reside in a mystical place known as Bandle City, though some of them have ventured out to live in Runeterra. Yordles are sometimes sexually dimorphic and rarely exceed 1 meter tall. Their skin texture ranges from being lightly covered in fur, to moderately fuzzy, to excessively bushy. Their hands have four digits while their feet differ greatly. Their fur tones are colourful. Their large eyes feature a large, circular iris with a vertically oval pupil, and have inferior vision in the normal spectrum of light. Yordles have much better hearing, due to their large fox-like ears and see into the infrared spectrum of light. Yordles age differently due to being creatures of the spirit realm and they don't die. Yordles don't breathe. Due to their physiology, yordles are vulnerable to be captured inside cages made of Runic Iron. Touching Runic Iron gives yordles an electrical-like shock, and will disrupt their magic. Yordles are adept at blending in.

entries.name: Vastaya
entries.content: Vastaya are chimeric race with countless of Subspecies and are usually humanoid with animal features. vastaya can look considerably different from one another, but they all share animal and human characteristics. They populate all of Runeterra, the animals they resemble depend on the kind of climate they live in. The Vastaya are inherently magical and tied heavily to the use of spirit magic. Disregarding distinctions between the tribes of land, sea, and air, there are three types of vastaya: Animal-like vastaya resemble other animals, but are bipedal or otherwise mildly humanoid. Human-like vastaya closely resemble humans, but still retain a modest level of animalistic elements. And the Shapeshifters retain either a human or animal appearance of their choosing, but they are able to shapeshift in and out of each form.

entries.name: Golem
entries.content: Whether organic or inorganic in origin, Golems are artificial constructs designed or inevitably created by sentient hands to provide a tireless aide for the plethora of purposes it was made for, usually combining multiple capabilities for a multitude of work or a focused specialty otherwise unachievable by a normal person. Golems are made with either a semblance of intelligence or full-fledged sentience, although creation of them are frowned upon by people for reasons ranging from ethical to moral.

entries.name: Revenant
entries.content: Revenants are souls that were bound to an object in the physical world. This object can either be their old body, hold together by magic, or a vessel like armor, a diving suit or even temporarily sand. Known revenants are Sahn-Uzal, Nautilus and the Bloodharbor Ripper.

entries.name: Wraith
entries.content: Wraiths are the predominant undead found on the Shadow Isles. These twisted spirits are remnants of their former selves that were ripped away from their living bodies by the Black Mist that oozed out of the Ruined King's broken heart. The stronger a Wraith's sense of self is, the stronger it will be as a result. Higher Wraiths, who have a strong enough sense of self, can take on a corporeal form after death, regaining some or all of the features they once had. Lower Wraiths, Mistwraiths, can not take on a corporeal form on their own and instead became an amalgamation of souls without a form. However, some of them are not aggressive. An innocent with a good heart who lands on the Shadow Isles may be met by a spectre with a benevolent or empathetic nature, who will try to lead the person to safety.

entries.name: Primary Magic
entries.content: The primary forms of magic are identified by what realm they draw their powers from and are as follow: Elemental Magic, Spirit Magic and Celestial Magic.

entries.name: Elemental Magic
entries.content: Elemental Magic control of the elements by drawing on the energies of the Material Realm. Though a large amount of elemental mages are naturally-born, it is a teachable art. Elemental magic can grant users the capability to manipulate all things in the physical realm ranging from basic raw elements such as fire or water to more theoretical ones such as time. Known Forms of Elemental Magic is Air, Electricity, Fire, Ice, Water, Light, Rock, Nature, Magma, Metal (Ferromancy), Sound and Time (Chronomancy).

entries.name: Spirit Magic
entries.content: Spirit Magic draws on the natural magical energies of the Spirit Realm. In order to utilize spirit magic, one must bring their souls closer to the spirit realm. The Vastaya are inherently magical and tied heavily to the use of spirit magic. By using spirit magic, mages can commune with certain Spirits or tap into the spiritual life essence of all things, living or otherwise, in nature. Spirit magic is typically unpredictable and chaotic. Known Forms of Spirit Magic is Soul, Ruination, Shadow, Fae, Dream, and Paint.

entries.name: Celestial Magic
entries.content: Celestial Magic is not entirely understood on Runeterra. Celestial magic draws energy from entire concepts of the universe, ranging from celestial bodies such as the sun to intangible ideas like war. Those utilizing celestial magic are granted many powers typically associated with the concept that their magic derives from. Celestial magic is immensely powerful and difficult to fully grasp for mortals, as it practically allows a user to completely distort reality to an extent. Aspect make use of Celestial Magic.

entries.name: Combined Magic
entries.content: Primary forms of magic are capable of being combined or used in unison, creating a large array of different magical forms. Combined Magic forms as follows: Ascended magic, Combination of Celestial and Elemental magics; Runic magic, Combination of Celestial and Elemental magics; Blood magic (Hemomancy), Combination of Elemental and Spiritual magics; Healing magic, Hextech, combination of Elemental and Spiritual mixed with technology.

entries.name: Blood magic
entries.content: Blood Magic is characterized by the ability to manipulate the spiritual essence of living things through their physical bodies, being capable of reshaping flesh and blood. This is largely used by the Crimson Circle. By manipulating flesh and blood of living beings, users can reshape the physical forms of themselves and others, absorb the life essence found in others' blood, prolong lifespans and control the bodies of others by puppeteering their flesh.

entries.name: Runic magic
entries.content: Runic magic is characterized by the unique feature of having to be written with special symbols and words that grant power. It has been shown to be capable of granting the ability to fire out blasts of arcane energy along the runes, enchant objects with runic writing to empower them and can even prolong one's lifespan.

entries.name: Ascended magic
entries.content: Ascended is pivotal in the creation of the Ascended by fusing their mortal bodies with the energies of the Celestial Realm, allowing them to reshape their physical forms, prolong their lifespans, empower their base abilities as well as grant them access to certain celestial magics.

entries.name: Marai
entries.content: The Marai are a water dwelling form of a sentient species known as the Vastaya. They resemble a mix between Humans and fish (humanoid upper part, fish lower part), the Marai are capable of withstanding enormous pressures of the ocean and being able to live in salt and fresh waters. Their distinct features are their uniquely formed scales and flaps. Their darker green scales end at the point of their chests, resembling clothing. Male Marai have their lighter scales shown more prominent in their chest area. Female Marai have larger and more prominent flaps around their bodies. Both sexes have flap protrusions resembling hair on their heads. These protrusions can be in various shades of yellow and green. Their eyes have dark sclera and irises in various shades of green, red, yellow, orange, and blue. Each Marai is trained to hunt from a young age. Not many surface people know of the Marai. They are considered as mythical creatures by sailors.

entries.name: Vesani
entries.content: The Vesani are a land dwelling form of a sentient species known as the Vastaya. They resemble a mix between humans and foxes, having vulpine-like traits such as big bushy tails, claws, and a pair of fox-like ears. Their nine tails can be grouped together to appear as only one tail. They have whisker-like markings on their cheeks. If not properly trained to control their hunger, a Vesani is able to completely absorb a person's life energy leaving them as drained husks. The Vesani have the unique ability to manipulate emotions and memories. They are also a nomadic tribe, traveling from land to land.

entries.name: Boleham
entries.content: Boleham is a city-state located on the slopes of the Argent Mountains in central Valoran. It borders with Noxus to the south. A group of people, for a time, lived under the reign of multiple sorcerers and warlords. These fiends caused many problems for the local people until they were defeated by Veigar.

entries.name: Arbormark
entries.content: The Arbormark are a nation in central Runeterra Crest icon Valoran, bordering Demacia, the Freljord, the Skaggorn and the Rijenland. The Arbormark are a longstanding ally of Demacia. During the Mage Rebellion which plunged Demacia into chaos, Arbormark delegates were summoned to aid the nation in its desperate time. It is notable that they appear to be apathetic to Demacia's treatment of mages, but they are completely accepting of mages themselves. The Arbormark Salute is performed with an individual touching the palm of their left hand to their forehead then extending it to the sky. Afterwards the individual present themselves and end with a head bow. Arbormark is governed by the Lord of Arbormark.

entries.name: Skaggorn
entries.content: The Skaggorn are a free nation located in central Valoran bordered by the Freljord, the Arbormark and Rijenland. A group of people left the Freljord many generations ago, traveling over the mountains and settling in Skaggorn. The old blood still runs in their veins, having seers with magical abilities. Mothers put runes on their children as a mark of protection. Asta, a Skaggorn woman and the the chieftain’s daughter, married a Demacian named Malak Hornbridge.

entries.name: Rijenland
entries.content: Rijenland is a nation that borders Demacia, Arbormark, Skaggorn and Nockmirch. Rijenland is one of the independent nations in central Valoran that Demacia maintains good relations with. Quinn Quinn notes their terrain is heavily wooded in the east, with no notable settlements in the area. They maintain peaceful relations with their neighbors, and trade with the Nockmirch. They only have a weak military force. There have been conflicts between the Nockmirch and Rijenland in the past. There are still smaller disputes, especially concerning hunting on the other side of the border, but their bond has been strengthened over generations. Their border is a natural barrier, a deep ravine over which the Nockmirch recently built a strong bridge and road. They could easily invade Rijenland. It is in Demacia's interest to ensure the independence of the nations to its east, and so it maintains friendly relations with Rijenland.

entries.name: Nockmirch
entries.content: Nockmirch is a nation and region located in central Valoran with Alderburg with it's capital. It is one of many nations bordering between Demacia and Noxus. The current leadership of the nation is a hereditary Lordship, with other positions taking care of other political aspects.

entries.name: Alderburg
entries.content: Alderburg is the presumed capital of Nockmirch. It is situated next to the ravine of Gray Claws

entries.name: Gray Claws
entries.content: The Gray Claws is a ravine that forms the natural border between Rijenland and Nockmirch. At the bottom of the Gray Claws flows a river of the same name, which eventually merges into the Silverrun River. The river has a lot of exposed rock, making it almost impossible to navigate through.

entries.name: Holdrum
entries.content: Holdrum is a coastal city-state in southern Valoran. It borders Noxus to the north, and Piltover and Zaun to the southwest. Piltover trading families have close trading ties with the city-state nation of Holdrum, such as Clan Medarda with Lord Brannin of Sea. One of the nations more well known exports to Piltover are pearls and fish sauce.

entries.name: Kalstead
entries.content: Klastead is a coastal fortified nation in south Valoran, bordering Demacia and Noxus. Kalstead have long been allies of Demacia. As a small nation between Demacia and Noxus, they have been instrumental in protecting the kingdoms borders.

entries.name: Palclyff
entries.content: Palclyff is a coastal city-state in western Valoran. It closely borders both Demacia and Noxus. Palclyff is a sought after trade city with great hospitality (except for Noxians) and strange local sports. Honeyfruits are a type of edible plant harvested near the city of Palcyff. Its healing properties are also used for medicinal purposes such as Health potions. Being a semi-aquatic plant, it can be seen on the shores of rivers, lakes, and other bodies of fresh water. Demacia has long protected neighboring city-states and nations from onslaught of invading armies such as Noxus. No citizen of Noxus is permitted to set foot on the shores of Palclyff and no exceptions are made. Piltover trading families have close trading ties with the city-state nation of Palclyff, such as Clan Medarda with Foreman Piarre Yaeshiff.

entries.name: Dalamor Plain
entries.content: Dalamor Plain is located at the northern edge of Noxus. Many travelers have lost their lives in this unforgiving wasteland. Due to the dusty climate and perhaps also the presence of a certain murderous yordle and his mythic drakalops, most Noxians avoid traveling through the area, with its only populated settlement for hundreds of miles being the village of Drugne.

entries.name: Drugne
entries.content: Drugne is an isolated town north of the Dalamor Plain and southeast of the Ironspike Mountains. It's rulership is a Noxian Stewardship.

entries.name: Ironspike Mountains
entries.content: The Ironspike Mountains are located in the northern part of Valoran. They border with Freljord and Noxus. The Ironspike Mountains run in a rough crescent, from their northern slopes in the Freljord to their eastern extremity along the coast of the sea, just north of Noxus. A Noxian colony was formed at its southern slopes called Delverhold.

entries.name: Delverhold
entries.content: The Delverhold is a fortified settlement of the Ironspike Mountains between Noxus and the cold tundra of the Freljord. Mountain fortress, whose rich mines supply Noxus with gold and iron. It was originally a kingdom of its own independence, that is until the empire of Noxus encroached about eighty-seven years ago. In fear of annihilation, the Delverhold king relinquished his authority and swore loyalty to Noxus. Now its people work endlessly to supply Noxus with armor and weapons crafted with the iron they mine; and in turn, are never drafted to fight for the empire. Alyssa Roshka Gloriana val-Lokan is the current Steward of Delverhold.

entries.name: Kimir
entries.content: Kimir is a Noxian mining city in northern Valoran. The city is currently led by Steward Colm Onren and is the leading exporter of Noxian granite in the north. Kimir's walls and battlements are made of fine stone, hewn and laid by Kimir's progenitors, as Kimirians are skilled sculptors and miners. The cities quarries were manned for generations by its able-bodied men and women, everyone who can drive a pick took shifts mining stone. This produced tall and strong individuals which were impressive even for Noxian standards. Terrain advantage and the Kimir's willingness to trade kept the city free for decades until the Noxian empire took over. Kimir deeply respects the fallen, erecting statues in their honor along with a proper funeral. This tradition is highly treasured, its negligence leading to a short rebellion against the Noxian warhost.

entries.name: Morrin
entries.content: Morrin is a Noxian town located in northern Valoran. Close to Kimir, their neighbors flowers were highly coveted by Morrin. A well-placed bundle of blue stargazer flowers won a war in the past between Kimir and Morrin before it began. After Kimir was conquered by Noxus, its warbands later came to conquer Morrin as well.

entries.name: Urtis
entries.content: Urtis is a northern frontier settlement of Noxus. It was previously its own independent kingdom until its king was killed by Darius. Urtis was governed by a king that was ruthless against his subjects, so much so that he had numerous slaves that were demanded to be obedient. With the arrival of Noxus, Urtis and its land belongs to the Empire.

entries.name: Bloodcliffs
entries.content: Bloodcliffs is a coastal city in eastern Noxus. Built into the cliffs near an estuary, Bloodcliff neighbors the Immortal Bastion and Basilich on the eastern coast of Valoran. The city's current leader is Steward Hovri IV. One of its main sources of trade are rough grades, which are used for establishing foundations of buildings.

entries.name: Khom
entries.content: Khom was a village located in what is today eastern Noxus. Birthplace of Ryze, this village was completely obliterated during the Rune Wars. Forever haunted by the devastation he witnessed during the Rune Wars, Ryze has sworn never to allow such power to be wielded again.

entries.name: Argent Mountains
entries.content: The Argent Mountains is a vast mountain range located in the southwestern part of Valoran and in southern Noxus. Noxus controls a small portion of the mountain range on its south-eastern and south-western parts. Its coastline has Noxian conquered settlements of Glorft, Kilgrove, Trevale. The mountain range borders close to the Varju Mountains on the east and the Gates of Mourning on the west. Bellswayer is a proud, celestial creature native to the Argent Mountains, the Bellswayer's beautiful chiming bells inspire and compel other sprites to attend them. Though they startle easily, bellswayers are just as quick to resume a composed and regal posture.

entries.name: Varju Mountains
entries.content: Varju Mountains is a mountain range bordering the Argent Mountains in the west, and The Great Barrier in the east of southern Noxus. Rokrund Plains are located at the footholds of the Vajru Mountains.

entries.name: The Great Barrier
entries.content: The Great Barrier is a mountain range located inside Noxus, in south-east Valoran. The cities of Basilich and Vindor is near its slopes. Numerous Minotaur clans reside all across the Great Barrier.

entries.name: Gates of Mourning
entries.content: Gates of Mourning are located in the southwestern tip Noxus and central Valoran. They were used to guard the neighboring lands from Noxian invasion before their recent fall. They are also located west of Hvardis. The Gates are the location of the first battles between Demacia and Noxus. In modern times it was retaken by the Trifarian Legion.

entries.name: Glorft
entries.content: Glorft is a settlement located south of the Argent Mountains on the coast.

entries.name: Hvardis
entries.content: Hvardis was a fortified city located at the edge of the Argent Mountains near the Gates of Mourning. Hvardis was the location of one of the first clashes between Noxus and Demacia. It was leveled to the ground by Swain's orders.

entries.name: Kilgrove
entries.content: Kilgrove is a coastal settlement south of the Argent Mountains in southern Noxus. Kilgrove is currently led by Steward Dauvin, who seems to have replaced his predecessor Thomark quite recently. Its primary export is Kilgrovian cloudcedar.

entries.name: Trevale
entries.content: Trevale is a collection of coastal settlements and farming communities located south of the Argent Mountains in southwestern Noxus. A collection of farming villages clinging to the rocky hillside, it is located in the western edge of Noxian territory. Kled was part of the initial Noxian party that sacked the village. Riven was born and raised here.

entries.name: Rokrund
entries.content: Rokrund is a coastal settlement of the Rokrund Plains in southern Noxus. The closest settlement is neighboring Qualthala. Rokrund is currently governed by steward Katye. Its primary export is the naap, a type of twisting root vegetable.

entries.name: Qualthala
entries.content: Qualthala is a coastal settlement located at the edge of the Rokrund Plains in southern Noxus.

entries.name: Basilich
entries.content: Basilich is located in southern Noxus at the footholds of The Great Barrier. Port city whose rebellion against the empire was quashed by its very own son, Darius. Located on the eastern coast of Valoran is the port city Basilich, which was integrated into the Noxian Empire after the city's elders submitted to Captain Cyrus and his army. Nowadays Basilich has been among a few cities that have attempted to rebel from the hold of Noxus. Most recently when the city's steward Quilletta Varn lost her faith in the Empire and sparked a revolution for independence. For acts of defiance, the city was besieged personally by the Hand of Noxus, Darius, who was also raised on the streets of Basilich as an orphan. The ongoing rebellion ended after the steward was murdered and replaced by Quilletta's second-in-command and daugther, Invetia Varn. The city is well known for its paintings made out of cobwebs.

entries.name: Ironwater
entries.content: Ironwater is a coastal settlement in southern Noxus. Located on the coast of the Guardian's Sea and east of Trannit, Ironwater is currently governed by steward Arron. Its primary export is beet wine.

entries.name: Krexor
entries.content: Krexor is a coastal settlement in southern Noxus. Located east of Piltover, it is governed by Steward Lisabetya, the latest in a long list of governors. The city is known for its Minotaur smiths.

entries.name: Trannit
entries.content: Trannit is a coastal settlement near the shores of the Guardian's Sea and west of Ironwater, in southeastern Noxus. Trannit is currently governed by steward Eranolaj Smik. It primarily exports dried Bolbo fish, which can be made into a local delicacy, boiled Bolbo-head soup.

entries.name: Vindor
entries.content: Vindor is a coastal settlement in southeastern Noxus, south of Basilich and west of the Fallgren islands. It is currently governed by Steward Amenesce. The city is well known for its Light Vindoran horse breed, bred for desert use. The Noxian Dark Riders are said to specifically only ride breeds from this area. More recently, when Basilich's steward, Quilleta Varn asked for help on her rebellion, Amenesce sent ships with a thousand of his best warriors. However, those warriors were going against Basilich, due to a thousand legionaries being camped within his city. The rebellion ended after Invertia Varn, the second in command, killed Quilleta.

entries.name: Fallgren
entries.content: Fallgren is one of two Noxian islands located off the coast of Basilich. The island city of Fallgren has been under control by Noxus ever since the Battle of Fallgren, purportedly spearheaded by Kled. Presently the city is governed by Steward Ieon. Many tubes used in Zaun have been made here by Hedicila Elastica.

entries.name: Navori
entries.content: Navori is an Ionian region and province that spans the western half of the Ionian Mainland of the Ionian Archipelago. It is considered the most populous region of Ionia, being the home to various villages, prestigious schools, sacred magical gardens, and the iconic Placidium of Navori. After the invasion, the southwestern tip of Navori is currently controlled by Noxus. It's also the location of Ionia City, the capital of Ionia. The Capital is the seat of power for the Ionian Ruling Council which members include Karma and Irelia.

entries.name: Sentinels of Light
entries.content: The Sentinels of Light are an order of warriors historically part of the Fellowship of Light, a society based in the Blessed Isles. Originating from a forgotten time when marauders threatened the Isles' peaceful settlements, their sworn duty was to safeguard against such assaults by using weapons created from ancient relic stones. After the Ruination of Helia had unfolded, Jenda'kaya, the last remaining Sentinel, reshaped the organization's purpose. No longer confined to the newly dubbed Shadow Isles, the Sentinels were reborn to defend Runeterra from the Wraiths that now haunt the Isles and threaten the rest of the world. Their objective is to free all Wraiths on the Shadow Isles from their unlife, Restoring the Blessed Isles and defend Runeterra from the Wraiths of the Shadow Isles.

entries.name: Azure Farms
entries.content: Azure Farms are a coastal area in Navori region of Ionia.

entries.name: Garden of Forgetting
entries.content: Garden of Forgetting, or the Garden of Dreaming, is located somewhere in the southern parts of the Navori region of Ionia. Its keeper is Ighilya, also known as the Eater of Secrets, the Forgotten, or the Witch Gardener. The flowers and the fruit of the Garden have deep magical properties that can take away a person's memories or life essence. The Dreaming Tree grew from a seed of the God-Willow, which towered over the ancient grove of Omikayalan.

entries.name: Omikayalan
entries.content: Omikayalan, known also as the Heart of the World or the Greenglade, is a sacred grove to all Ionians which was located in Navori. The vastayashai'rei protected its most important landmark, the God-Willow, a massive tree, dripping with long gossamer leaves that shimmered with golden-green light. During ancient times, a battle between the groves protectors and Freljordian warriors ended with the God-Willow's destruction. The whimpers of countless beasts, the bawling of rivers, the howling of trees and the dripping tears of moss, they lamented the God-Willow's death in a symphony of mourning. Centuries have passed and at the place where the God-Willow once stood, a being known as the Green Father Green Father emerged with a clear mission and purpose: to protect all life and teach the world's people to respect and appreciate all that is. Omikayalan's sapling is guarded by a group of secretive Vastaya lords.

entries.name: Placidium of Navori
entries.content: The Placidium of Navori is a sacred site of Ionian Harmony. Located in the Navori region of the Ionian Mainland, the Placidium is one of the First Lands' most sacred places. Over countless centuries, Ionians have journeyed here to study at renowned schools, or meditate in its wild, magical gardens. Many of Ionia's most successful diplomats have spent at least some time studying at the Placidium.

entries.name: Thanze
entries.content: Thanze is a city located in Southeastern Navori. It was ravaged by the Noxian Invasion of Ionia. The Navori Brotherhood and Zed's Shadow Order defended this city and its inhabitants.

entries.name: Weh'le
entries.content: Weh'le is a hidden coastal village located at the southern area of the Navori region of Ionia. It borders with Noxian controlled Navori. Weh'le is a phantom port, a hidden coastal village, protected by the mystical properties of Ionia. Unlike Fae'lor, she doesn't welcome outsiders, and you won't find her on the maps. Should Weh'le appear at all, it is always on her own terms, daring people into doing very dumb things. Most approach from the sea, dreaming of riches, discovery or maybe just a new start, only to have their hopes dashed in an instant. First, the shoreline that once called to them vanishes behind a dense wall of cobalt fog crackling with arcane power.

entries.name: Bel'zhun
entries.content: Bel'zhun is a coastal city and outpost in northern Shurima (or Shuriman Noxus), known for its thriving black markets and signature mwatis wool. This northern city is currently controlled by Noxus, but has a large rebel insurgency against Noxus. Known as the Suns of Bel'Zhun, the group frequently trades weapons with Clan Medarda of Piltover.

entries.name: Tereshni
entries.content: Tereshni is a port city located in northern Shurima, currently controlled by Noxus. This Shuriman port city is currently controlled by Noxus and led by Steward Ta'Fik. The city's best-known export is Shuriman Azirite (aka blood glass), named after the current Shuriman Emperor, Azir.

entries.name: Urzeris
entries.content: Urzeris is a coastal city of northern Shurima, now currently occupied by Noxus. Its current governor is Steward Zikka Taum'Vin. Its most well known trade good is Urzeris Salt. Marcus Du Couteau with his family was stationed close to the governor of Uzeris before his assassination. Both Katarina and Cassiopeia lived here during their younger years.

entries.name: Lunari
entries.content: Lunari are an ancient organization and religious order which task is to venerate the Aspect of the Moon of Mount Targon. Rakkor are the natives of Mount Targon. Both the Solari and Lunari religious orders originate from this tribe. Branded by the Solari as heretics, the Lunari worship the silvery light of the moon. They practice their beliefs in secret, hiding from the Solari who seek to rid Targon of their influence forever. Long ago, the two groups lived in peace, worshipping the heavens as one people. The Lunari chart celestial movements to divine the future. Certain priestesses wear necklaces of mirrored moonglass. Some Lunari seers bind their eyes during the day, training their eyes to see only in darkness, for only under the pure light of the moon is truth revealed. The weapons mainly used by the Lunari are made of moonsilver, silver metal forged in moonlight which imbues with a touch of magic. Some of them are also made of moonstones which are super-rare stones from a piece of the moon that broke off and embedded in the mountain aeons ago and are evidently much more potent magically than moonsilver. The Lunari do not have any hatred or contempt for the Solari, although they do not hesitate to defend themselves if necessary. Lunari may use Crescent Guardian in battle, a Construct made by the Lunari and Enhanced by the full moon. Some Lunari roles include theLunari Cultist, Lunari Duskbringer, Lunari Priestes and Moondreamers who Interprets the stars and constellations.

entries.name: Solari
entries.content: Solari are an ancient organization and religious order which task is to venerate the Aspect of the Sun of Mount Targon. Rakkor are the natives of Mount Targon. Both the Solari and Lunari religious orders originate from this tribe. The worship of the Sun as the source of all life. Solaric worship is largely made up by a special sect of Rakkorians who surrender their mantles of war in favor of greater solar devotion. Their founder and leader chose Mount Targon, being the highest peak closest to the Sun, and was blessed with the power to call down the sun's wrath. Currently, Leona, the Radiant Dawn, has taken this legend's regalia and fights to protect the helpless and the innocent. While nearly all Rakkor worship the sun, those who completely devote their lives to it are known as the Solari. As the dominant religious sect on Mount Targon, they believe the sun is the source of all life, all other light sources are false, and a threat to the future of their people. Disciples are guided in the strictures of their faith by temple priests, who preach that if the sun was ever to fade, the world would be swallowed by darkness. The Ra'Horak, a Rakkor title which means Followers of the Horizon, honed their already fearsome skills with a blade into something sublime. As Elite warriors of the Solari, they practice for years under the harshest conditions and less susceptible to the cold. The Solari elders claimed Leona from the Rakkor tribe and assisted in focusing her abilities. Scribes and acolytes sometimes spend the winter months sheltering in the relative warmth of the Solari temples, conducting divine rituals to call upon the power of the sun and charting the movements of the stars. During times of strife, a Solari priest might meditate in the outermost sanctum for weeks without food or water, subsisting merely on the divine sustenance of the sun, the source of all life. Solari may use Sun Guardians in combat, a construct made by the Solari. Solari roles may include the Solari Priestess, Solari Sentinel from the Sentinels of Light, Solari Shieldbearer, Solari Soldier and Solari Sunforger.

entries.name: Rakkorians
entries.content: Rakkor are the main tribal faction and natives of Mount Targon. Both the Solari and Lunari religious orders originate from this tribe. Rakkor tribes boast many skilled artisans, craftspeople, and merchants, however, they tend to value a simple life of humility and prayer to the heavens. Rakkor tribe dwells at the very limits of human endurance; honing their warrior skills to fight the war at the end of the world. Rakkor means Tribe of the Last Sun, and its people believe that many worlds have existed before this one. Its seers teach that when this sun is destroyed there will be no more, so its warriors must be ready to fight those who seek to extinguish its light. All members of the tribe are expected to fight and kill without mercy or hesitation. Rakkor warriors are trained not only to be as lethal with their bare hands as the most capable martial artists, but also to fiercely wield the many relic-weapons of the tribe. While nearly all the Rakkor worship the sun, those who devoted are known as the Solari. Those known as the Lunari secretly worship the light of the moon. They keep their beliefs hidden from the Solari, who greatly outnumber them and see them as dangerous heretics.
